blocks.text: Quick verdict

Decodo is the better proxy network: a 115M+ advertised pool, city, ZIP and ASN targeting, sticky sessions, near-perfect independent success rates and scraping APIs for harder sites. Proxy-Cheap is the better price: about $7.80 for 10 GB at its promotional rate against $35 at Decodo, with no plan required. For easy or moderate targets where country targeting is enough, Proxy-Cheap saves real money. For hardened sites, location-specific data or anything where failed requests are costly, Decodo is worth it.

Decodo and Proxy-Cheap are two of the most common answers to the question of which residential proxy to buy on a budget, but they sit at different price points. Proxy-Cheap is currently advertising $0.78/GB with no subscription. Decodo costs several times more but offers a large published pool, city and ZIP targeting, and benchmark success rates near 99.9%. This comparison works out whether Decodo's quality is worth the premium for your targets, or whether Proxy-Cheap's price wins.

blocks.text: Decodo in 2026: what you get

Decodo is the 2024 rebrand of Smartproxy, one of the most popular mid-market providers. Its residential network is advertised at 115 million IPs across 195+ locations, and independent benchmarks put its success rate around 99.9% with sub-second response times. Every plan includes the full pool plus city, state, ZIP and ASN targeting, and the dashboard is one of the easiest to set up. Decodo also sells datacenter, ISP and mobile proxies and a family of scraping APIs.

Strengths: Large 115M+ pool at a mid-market price; Near-perfect success rates in independent tests; Clean, fast self-service onboarding; Scraping APIs available when raw proxies are not enough. Weak spots: Plan traffic does not roll over; Published pricing stops at 100 GB; beyond that you need a quote; More expensive per GB than budget brands.
Proxy-Cheap in 2026: what you get

Proxy-Cheap lives up to its name: rotating residential traffic is currently advertised at $0.78/GB (70% off a $2.60 list price) with no subscription, and static ISP and datacenter IPs cost a dollar or two per month. The catalog is broad, covering IPv6 options few competitors offer, and payment by card, PayPal, Alipay or crypto is easy. The trade-offs are thinner targeting (country and ISP rather than city on rotating residential) and less published performance data than the bigger brands.

Strengths: Very low per-GB price while the promotion runs; No monthly commitment on rotating residential; Broad catalog including IPv6 and static mobile; SOCKS5 with UDP support. Weak spots: Targeting is mostly country and ISP, not city; Residential pool size not separately published; Mixed results in some independent benchmarks.
Pricing: Decodo vs Proxy-Cheap

Decodo sells residential traffic at $4/GB pay-as-you-go with no commitment, or on monthly plans: 3 GB for $11.25 ($3.75/GB), 10 GB for $35, 25 GB at $3.25/GB, 50 GB for $150 and 100 GB for $275 ($2.75/GB). Top-ups are billed at your plan's rate, so you are not pushed into the next tier.

Proxy-Cheap's rotating residential proxies are pay-as-you-go, currently listed from $0.78/GB (a promotional price against a $2.60/GB list rate). Static residential ISP proxies start around $2.44 per IP per month, datacenter IPv4 at about $1.49, datacenter IPv6 from $0.15, and rotating mobile at $5.99/GB.

Buying 10 GB, you would pay about $7.80 with Proxy-Cheap and $35 with Decodo: a 78% saving in Proxy-Cheap's favour. At 100 GB a month, Proxy-Cheap is the cheaper option at about $78 against $275 for Decodo, roughly 72% less. Both Decodo and Proxy-Cheap work on allowances that do not carry forward indefinitely, so size your plan to real monthly usage rather than buying ahead.
Pool size, coverage and targeting

Proxy-Cheap does not publish a clear residential pool figure, so a size comparison is not possible on published data. Decodo lists '115M+' and Proxy-Cheap lists 'Not separately published (155M+ claimed across all products)'. In practice, what matters is how many unique IPs you get in the countries you target, which you can measure in a short trial by sending a few thousand requests and counting distinct exit addresses. For coverage, Decodo lists 195+ countries and Proxy-Cheap lists 180+. On targeting, Decodo offers country, state, city, ZIP and ASN, while Proxy-Cheap offers country and ISP.
Protocols, sessions and setup

Both providers support SOCKS5 as well as HTTP(S), so either will plug into scrapers, anti-detect browsers and automation tools that expect a SOCKS endpoint. On sessions, Decodo offers rotating or sticky sessions with configurable duration, and Proxy-Cheap offers rotating and sticky sessions. Both use a backconnect gateway: you point your tool at one host and port, and choose country, city or session behaviour through parameters in the username.
Which is better for your use case?

General web scraping: Decodo wins. The deciding factor for Decodo: a large pool and near-perfect benchmark success rates. The limitation on the Proxy-Cheap side: cheap traffic, though independent benchmark results have been mixed.

SERP and rank tracking: Decodo wins. The deciding factor for Decodo: a dedicated SERP scraping API plus city targeting. The limitation on the Proxy-Cheap side: workable for light rank tracking at a low cost.

Social media and multi-account management: tie. Neither has a clear edge. With Decodo: sticky sessions, sub-users and an easy dashboard. With Proxy-Cheap: cheap static ISP and mobile IPs for persistent identities. Run the same small test on both before committing.
E-commerce price and stock monitoring: Decodo. Decodo has the edge here. Why: ZIP targeting and a ready-made e-commerce API. How Proxy-Cheap compares: fine for country-level price checks.
Ad verification and geo-testing: Decodo. Decodo has the edge here. Why: wide coverage with city and ASN targeting. How Proxy-Cheap compares: lacks city-level targeting on rotating residential.
Tight budgets: Proxy-Cheap wins. The deciding factor for Proxy-Cheap: the lowest advertised per-GB price in this pairing. The limitation on the Decodo side: it is mid-priced, not cheap.
Trials, verification and billing fine print

Before you pay, check how each provider lets you test. Decodo: Free trial (about 100 MB) on residential. Proxy-Cheap: 7-day $1.99 trial on static residential and datacenter IPs. Verification and payment rules differ too. Decodo: Light KYC; checks on some targets. Proxy-Cheap: Light; card, PayPal, Alipay and crypto accepted. Whichever you choose, measure cost per successful request rather than cost per gigabyte: retries, blocked pages and heavy page assets all burn bandwidth, and a cheaper network that fails more often can end up costing more. Blocking images and fonts in your scraper, reusing sessions where a target allows it, and capping concurrency are the quickest ways to cut the bill on either provider.
How to test Decodo and Proxy-Cheap before you commit
The quickest way to choose between Decodo and Proxy-Cheap is a side-by-side test on the sites and countries you actually care about:
1. Buy the smallest option on each side (Decodo: free trial (about 100 MB) on residential; Proxy-Cheap: 7-day $1.99 trial on static residential and datacenter IPs).
2. Pick three to five real target URLs and the two or three countries that matter most, and send the same number of requests (a few hundred is enough) through each provider at the same time of day.
3. Record success rate, median response time, CAPTCHAs or blocks, and the number of unique exit IPs you received per country.
4. Divide what you spent by the number of successful, correctly located responses to get cost per useful request, then scale that to your monthly volume.
Bottom line

Across the six use cases above, Decodo comes out ahead in 4, Proxy-Cheap in 1, and 1 is a tie. That makes Decodo the safer default if you are unsure, but the right answer still depends on your volume and targets: Decodo is strongest for small and mid-size scraping teams, while Proxy-Cheap is strongest for price-sensitive scraping at moderate difficulty. If you can, spend a few dollars testing both on the exact sites and countries you care about; a one-hour test tells you more than any spec sheet.
Decodo is the better pick for:
Small and mid-size scraping teams
Developers who want enterprise-like quality without contracts
Mixed workloads that may grow into scraping APIs
Proxy-Cheap is the better pick for:
Price-sensitive scraping at moderate difficulty
Buyers who want static ISP or IPv6 IPs cheaply
Short projects that do not justify a monthly plan
